did: Home now has one way to deploy. Every server image says what it provides and what it needs of the others, and CI refuses a release whose images don't fit together. make home-deploy pulls the whole release, checks it again, brings it up from its own copy of the repo at the release's commit, waits for every service to be ready, and puts the whole previous release back if any one of them fails. The reconciler now follows file-host and render too, so publishing an image is enough to move it into the next release.

calls.title: What makes two commits the same release
options: A release is its serial plus the git trees of what compose reads: infra, deploy/home and docker-compose.yml
A release is its serial alone
calls.why: Three blocking review findings in a row came from the serial alone, so the shape was reshaped rather than patched again. The commit alone would restart services on every docs merge. The tree key re-applies a config change, leaves a docs merge alone, and lets a config fix be retried.
calls.undo: Key Target in apps/envctl/src/deploy.rs by release.serial or by commit instead of by the tree ids, and update RL11 in docs/release.md.

calls.title: Render waits for file-host's digest before the reconciler follows it
options: Follow render in R4, together with pinning file-host by digest
Follow render in R3, as #790 said
calls.why: While file-host was held on :latest the set check could not read its labels, so following render then would have let any render bump through unchecked, which is the break #756 was.
calls.undo: None needed now that both have landed.

left: A release that adds or drops a service leaves an orphan container running, and a rollback does not stop one the failed release added: #861.
The tree check misses relative bind mounts, and the real release-key lookup has no unit test: #863.
Epochs are met by a number at least as high, so a file_host that drops a layout an older render still reads is not refused; ranges are #859, the owner's call.
No Docker daemon was available, so it is unconfirmed that docker image inspect resolves a repo:tag@sha256 reference; home's first make home-deploy shows it.
